2027-04-02.title: Friday within the Octave of Easter
readings: There is salvation in no one else: there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved
The stone rejected by the builders has become the cornerstone (or: Alleluia)
Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and did the same with the fish
2027-04-02.alt: Day within the Octave of Easter, kept with the rank of a solemnity. The Gloria is sung; the Easter Sequence may be sung before the Gospel acclamation; the dismissal has the double Alleluia. Liturgical colour: white. Although it is a Friday, there is no abstinence today: every day of the Easter Octave has the rank of a solemnity (Code of Canon Law 1251). First Friday of the month. St Francis of Paola (2 April) is not observed this year. Eighth day of the Divine Mercy Novena.
2027-04-02.verse: That disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!”
theo: Peter and John are still speaking to the people in the Temple when the priests, the captain of the temple guard and the Sadducees arrive, “much annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming that in Jesus there is the resurrection of the dead.” The Sadducees did not believe in any resurrection at all, and here were two Galileans announcing that it had already begun in Jesus. The Apostles spend the night in custody. Yet Luke slips in a quiet line of victory: “many of those who heard the word believed; and they numbered about five thousand.” The word of God is not locked up with its preachers. The next morning the Temple leaders gather, Annas and Caiaphas among them, the same men before whom Jesus stood a few weeks earlier. Their question is the right one, though they ask it in the wrong spirit: “By what power or by what name did you do this?”

Then Peter, “filled with the Holy Spirit,” answers. This is the man who, on the night of the Passion, could not admit to a servant girl that he knew Jesus. Now he stands before the high priest and says: “this man is standing before you in good health by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead. This Jesus is ‘the stone that was rejected by you, the builders; it has become the cornerstone.’ There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.” The Psalm of the day sings the same verse that Peter quotes: “The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone. This is the LORD's doing; it is marvelous in our eyes.” The Church has always held this truth firmly: Jesus Christ is the one Saviour of the whole world. The Second Vatican Council adds that God's grace, which always comes through Christ, can reach in ways known to God those who through no fault of their own do not yet know him (Lumen Gentium 16). That is not a reason to be silent; it is a reason to speak his name with love, as Peter did.

The Gospel takes us back to Galilee, to the Sea of Tiberias. Seven disciples are together, and Simon Peter says simply, “I am going fishing.” They go with him, “but that night they caught nothing.” A long, empty night of work: many fishermen, many parents, many young people looking for a job know that night. “Just after daybreak, Jesus stood on the beach; but the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.” He calls to them as a father calls his children: “Children, you have no fish, have you?” They answer, “No.” He tells them to cast the net to the right side of the boat, and now they cannot haul it in for the number of fish. The beloved disciple sees with the eyes of love before anyone else: “It is the Lord!” Peter, impulsive as ever, puts on his clothes and jumps into the sea to reach him first.

On the shore a charcoal fire is already burning, with fish on it, and bread. The only other charcoal fire in John's Gospel is the one in the high priest's courtyard where Peter warmed himself and denied his Master (John 18:18). Now the Lord lights a new fire, of welcome. He asks for some of the fish they have caught, and Peter hauls the net ashore, “full of large fish, a hundred fifty-three of them; and though there were so many, the net was not torn.” Then come the gentlest words: “Come and have breakfast.” None of them dares ask, “Who are you?” They know. “Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and did the same with the fish.” The Fathers saw here a picture of the Church: the boat of Peter, the net that gathers every kind of people and does not tear, and the Lord who feeds his tired disciples with bread from his own hands. Without him the night is empty; with him the net is full, and breakfast is ready on the shore.
conn: A priestly party linked with the leading Temple families. They denied the resurrection of the dead (Luke 20:27; Acts 23:8); ancient writers say they held only the five books of Moses as binding. The Pharisees, by contrast, believed in the resurrection.

Annas had been high priest (AD 6–15) and remained powerful; Caiaphas, his son-in-law, was high priest from about AD 18 to 36 (John 18:13). These were particular leaders of the Temple; the five thousand who believed were also Jews.
In the Bible the name stands for the person and his authority. The whole of Acts 3–4 turns on “the name” of Jesus, mentioned again and again.
Psalm 118:22, quoted by Jesus himself (Mark 12:10) and by Peter again in 1 Peter 2:7. The stone thrown away by the builders becomes the stone that holds the whole building together.
Another name for the Sea of Galilee, from the city Herod Antipas built on its western shore in honour of the emperor Tiberius (John 6:1).
Jesus uses the tender word paidia, little ones, as a father speaks to his family.
The Greek word anthrakia appears only twice in the New Testament: at Peter's denial (John 18:18) and here (John 21:9). The scene prepares the threefold “Do you love me?” that follows (John 21:15–17).

Many explanations have been offered. St Jerome mentions a belief of his time that there were 153 kinds of fish, so the catch would stand for every nation; St Augustine saw in it the number of all who are saved. What is certain is John's point: a great catch, and a net that does not tear.
altar: On the shore the Risen Lord “took the bread and gave it to them.” At every Mass he does the same: he prepares the table, he is the host, and he himself is the food, truly present in the Bread of Life.

“Come and have breakfast.” After a night of empty nets, the Lord's first word is an invitation to eat with him. Come to Communion today not as one who has earned it, but as a tired child whom the Father calls to the fire.
outline: Ask: have you ever worked all night and caught nothing?
The new charcoal fire and the bread from his hands.
A full net on the sand that does not tear.
“There is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.”
live: Pray the name of Jesus slowly ten times today, in the bus, at work or in the kitchen, as an act of faith.
Take up again, with prayer, one task in which you have failed, and do it as the Lord asks.
Visit the Blessed Sacrament today and entrust your family to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
Like the Lord on the shore, prepare a meal or a cup of tea for someone who is tired.
fathers: St Augustine (Tractates on John 123, in substance)

The roasted fish is Christ who suffered. He is also the bread that came down from heaven. To this meal he invited the seven disciples, and in them all of us, so that we too may share in so great a sacrament and in so great a blessedness.
St Gregory the Great (Homily 24 on the Gospels, in substance)

Peter returned to fishing after the Resurrection, but Matthew did not return to collecting taxes. Work that can be done without sin may be taken up again after conversion; business that cannot be done without sin may not.
St Jerome (Commentary on Ezekiel 47, in substance)

Those who write about the nature of animals say that there are a hundred and fifty-three kinds of fish. All of them were caught by the Apostles, a sign that from every nation, noble and lowly, rich and poor, people are drawn up into the net of the Church.
magis: The name of Jesus is the divine name that alone brings salvation: “there is no other name under heaven” (Acts 4:12).

Outside the Church no salvation, rightly understood: all salvation comes from Christ through the Church; those who without fault do not know Christ can be saved; the Church still has the duty to evangelize.
Dominus Iesus 13–14 (Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, 2000)
Jesus Christ is the unique and universal Saviour; the Church must hold this firmly as a truth of faith.
Images of the Church: the sheepfold, the field, and the building whose cornerstone is Christ.
Those who seek God with a sincere heart and, moved by grace, try to do his will may attain salvation.
saints: Hermit and founder of the Order of Minims (1416–1507). His motto was Caritas, charity. He died at Tours, in France, on Good Friday, 2 April 1507. His optional memorial is not observed this year because of the Octave.

Died on 2 April 2005, the eve of Divine Mercy Sunday, the feast he had established for the whole Church in 2000. He was beatified and later canonized on Divine Mercy Sunday. His memorial is on 22 October.
2027-04-02.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, who gave us the Paschal Mystery in the covenant you established for reconciling the human race, so dispose our minds, we pray, that what we celebrate by professing the faith we may express in deeds. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, you stood on the shore at daybreak while your friends toiled in vain. Call to us in our empty nights, teach us to cast our nets at your word, and feed us at your fire with the bread of your own hands, so that with the beloved disciple we may say: It is the Lord! Alleluia. Amen.

quick: Peter before the council: the healed man stands here by the name of Jesus, the rejected stone made cornerstone.
There is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved.
At the Sea of Tiberias the Risen Lord fills the net and gives his disciples bread and fish.
2027-04-02.action: Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament this First Friday and say: “It is the Lord!”
2027-04-02.question: In which empty night of my life do I need to hear Jesus say: cast the net again?
catechism: Salvation in the name of Jesus alone.
Christ the cornerstone of the Church.
The name of Jesus contains all: God and man and the whole economy of salvation.
kidsaint: Francis loved God so much that he went to live alone in a cave when he was only a boy. Later many men joined him, and they lived very simply, eating no meat, to show their love for God. A story tells that once a boatman would not take him across the sea, so Francis spread his cloak on the water and crossed on it! His favourite word was “Charity,” which means love. Lesson: love is the most important word of all.
2027-04-02.special: Friday within the Octave of Easter (solemnity): Gloria; the Easter Sequence may be sung; double Alleluia at the dismissal. No Friday abstinence. First Friday of the month.
term: The Greek word for “fish.” Its letters were read as the first letters of “Iēsous Christos Theou Yios Sōtēr,” Jesus Christ, Son of God, Saviour. Early Christians drew a fish as a secret sign of their faith.

family.explain: Peter and his friends went fishing all night and caught nothing. In the morning a man on the shore told them to throw the net on the right side. Suddenly the net was full of big fish! John cried out: It is the Lord! Peter jumped into the water to reach him. Jesus had made a fire and cooked breakfast for them.
family.intention: We pray for fishermen and for all who work hard and are tired, that Jesus may bless their work.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family works very hard for us?” Make a small breakfast surprise for them tomorrow.

illus: In Fort Kochi an old man who mended the great fishing nets on the shore was teaching his grandson. The boy asked why the net did not tear when it was full. The old man showed him the knots: each one small, each one tied by hand, each one holding its neighbour. One knot alone holds nothing, he said, but a thousand knots together can lift the sea. Then he added: that is why we go to Mass together on Sunday. The Lord fills the net, and we hold one another.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen and standing on the shore of our lives, call to us, fill our nets and feed us with your bread. Alleluia. Amen.
share: By what power or by what name did you do this? (Acts 4:7). What would I answer if someone asked me why I live as I do?
That night they caught nothing (John 21:3). Where have I been working without the Lord?
Come and have breakfast (John 21:12). How do I answer the Lord's invitation to the Eucharist?
pm.resp: The stone rejected by the builders has become the cornerstone.
interc: For the Pope and the bishops, successors of Peter and the Apostles, that they may speak the name of Jesus with courage.
For all who seek God with a sincere heart, that they may come to know Christ the Saviour.
For fishermen and all who labour through the night, especially on the coasts of Kerala.
For families devoted to the Sacred Heart on this First Friday.
For our group, that we may recognize the Lord and say with joy: It is the Lord!
pm.close: Father, the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. Build us up on Christ, and make us one in the net of your Church. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the leaders of the Temple ask Peter and John a question: by what power or by what name did you do this? (Acts 4:7). It is a good question for every Christian. When people see us forgive, serve or hope, they should be able to ask: in whose name do you do this?

Peter answers with the courage of the Holy Spirit: by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead. A few weeks before, he was afraid of a servant girl. Now he is not afraid of the high priest. The Resurrection and the Spirit have changed him.

And Peter says: there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12). Jesus is not one teacher among many. He is the Saviour. That is why we pray in his name, are baptized in his name and live in his name.

In the Gospel the disciples have fished all night and caught nothing. Many of us know nights like that: work without fruit, prayers that seem unanswered, efforts that fail. At daybreak Jesus stands on the shore and calls: children, you have no fish, have you? He knows our empty nets.

He tells them to cast the net again, on the right side. They obey, and the net is full. The beloved disciple cries out: it is the Lord! (John 21:7). Love recognizes him first. When we obey his word, even in small things, we begin to see that he was with us all along.

On the shore the Lord has already prepared a fire and breakfast. He says: come and have breakfast. And he takes the bread and gives it to them. This is what he does at every Mass. Today, on this First Friday, let us come to him tired as we are, and let him feed us. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, the disciples fished all night and caught nothing. Jesus told them to try again, and the net was full of fish! John shouted: it is the Lord!
Then Jesus made breakfast for his friends. Jesus takes care of us too. Let us say: thank you, Jesus, for loving us!

intro: The name above every name, love that recognizes the Lord, and the breakfast he prepares on the shore.

sub: Prisoners, yet the word is not bound.
q: The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone.
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.
points.apply: Begin and end your work today with the sign of the cross, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

sub: “Children, you have no fish, have you?”
q: I am now sending for many fishermen, says the Lord, and they shall catch them;
That disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!”
points.apply: Look back on today before sleeping and name one moment when the Lord was with you without your noticing.

sub: A full net that does not tear.
q: On this mountain the Lord of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines, of rich food filled with marrow, of well-aged wines strained clear.
Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and did the same with the fish.
points.apply: Come to Mass this Sunday a little early, and spend those minutes thanking the Lord for the meal he prepares.

concl: Jesus is the one Saviour, and his name gives courage to the weakest disciple.
He meets us after our empty nights, fills our nets and feeds us from his own hands.
2027-04-02.resolve: Whenever something good happens this week, say in your heart: “It is the Lord!”
